source: Evaluation-only paraphrases derived from the course-supported concepts in validation_questions.json

questions.question: A person is recovering from a unilateral stroke. Which walking pattern is most characteristic?
options: A. The trunk shifts toward the weak side during stance
B. Weight is shifted toward the stronger side while the weak leg circumducts
C. The arms swing excessively while both legs flex normally
D. Both upper limbs are held in extension and both lower limbs in flexion
questions.rationale: Stroke gait: weight shift to the unaffected side with circumduction of the affected leg.

questions.question: After a stroke, a patient's left ankle joint cannot move. In the WHO terminology used in the course, what level does this finding describe?
options: A. Disability
B. Handicap
C. Impairment
D. Participation restriction
questions.rationale: An abnormal body function or structure, such as inability to move the ankle joint, is impairment.

questions.question: For upper-limb stroke rehabilitation, which combination is consistent with the course goals? I. Reduce spasticity. II. Suppress neuroplasticity. III. Inhibit atypical muscle synergies. IV. Let the unaffected arm perform every daily task.
options: A. II only
B. I and III only
C. I, III, and IV only
D. All four statements
questions.rationale: The course treats reducing spasticity and inhibiting atypical synergies as goals; reducing neuroplasticity and replacing all daily use with the healthy limb are not.

questions.question: Which set of claims agrees with the lecture's description of rehabilitation robots? I. They can deliver high-intensity training. II. They necessarily cause physical strain to the patient. III. They can provide range-of-motion and strengthening exercises. IV. They can be combined with virtual reality for activities-of-daily-living training.
options: A. I and III only
B. II only
C. I, III, and IV only
D. All four
questions.rationale: The slides support I, III, and IV; the statement that robot-assisted therapy causes physical strain is not a course benefit.

questions.question: An actuator contains an inflatable internal bladder inside a braided shell whose threads are flexible but non-extensible, and its contraction is controlled with compressed air. Which actuator is described?
options: A. Hydraulic actuator
B. Electric motor
C. Pneumatic Artificial Muscle
D. Hybrid electric actuator
questions.rationale: The bladder, braided mesh shell, and compressed-air actuation identify a Pneumatic Artificial Muscle.

questions.question: In the rehabilitation context, which statement best captures neuroplasticity after stroke?
options: A. Therapy mechanically deforms soft brain tissue
B. Previously unused motor areas may be activated to assume motor-control functions when properly stimulated
C. Every damaged motor area grows a replacement cell during training
D. Therapy restores blood vessels by exercising the limb
questions.rationale: The course describes recruitment of unused motor areas with appropriate stimulation, not guaranteed new cells or mechanical deformation.

questions.question: A patient has hemiparesis following a stroke. Which description is correct?
options: A. Weakness or partial paralysis affecting one side of the body
B. Paralysis of both legs only
C. Paralysis of both arms only
D. Paralysis of the left arm and right leg in every case
questions.rationale: Hemiparesis means weakness or partial paralysis on one side.

questions.question: A stroke caused by an obstruction in a cerebral blood vessel is classified as which mechanism?
options: A. Hemorrhagic stroke from vessel rupture
B. Traumatic brain injury
C. Ischemic stroke from reduced blood supply
D. Brain tumor
questions.rationale: A blockage reducing cerebral blood supply is the ischemic mechanism.

questions.question: In the three-level controller of a rehabilitation robot, which task belongs to the low-level controller?
options: A. Infer the user's movement intention
B. Decide between passive and active modes
C. Regulate accurate force output from joint actuators
D. Plan the overall therapy strategy
questions.rationale: Low-level control closes the actuator/joint loop and regulates accurate force output.

questions.question: Which activity is an example of a rehabilitation engineer's role described in the course?
options: A. Give the patient's family investment advice
B. Massage the patient's legs
C. Measure routine vital signs as a nurse
D. Evaluate the performance of the patient's prosthetic leg
questions.rationale: Testing prosthetic-leg performance is an engineering assessment task.

questions.question: What distinguishes an end-effector upper-limb rehabilitation robot?
options: A. It attaches at the distal part of the upper limb
B. It is restricted to chronic-stage patients
C. It is useful only for hand rehabilitation
D. It can be attached to only one limb
questions.rationale: The end-effector is the distal interface with the patient's upper limb.

questions.question: A person with cervical SCI retains head movement but little limb movement. According to the interface example in the course, can the person operate a six-DOF robotic arm?
options: A. Yes, through an indirect scanning interface
B. No, six inputs are impossible
C. Yes, but the arm must be limited to one DOF
D. Only if a caregiver directly moves every joint
questions.rationale: Residual head movement can be coupled to an indirect scanning mechanism to select commands for a multi-DOF arm.

questions.question: A teenager with cerebral palsy can move the hand and fingers but cannot control them accurately enough for small keys. Which typing aid directly addresses the precision problem?
options: A. One-switch keyboard with an arbitrary fixed scan time
B. Foot-pedal scanning keyboard
C. Enlarged keyboard with keys large enough for the available accuracy
D. A standard keyboard with no adaptation
E. Two-switch scanning keyboard
questions.rationale: The decisive clue is inaccurate hand/finger control: enlarged keys make the target easier to hit accurately.

questions.question: A screenshot shows an assistive-device interface whose selection set contains more than two choices. Is the statement true? (Image-dependent; do not score from text-only API input.)
options: A. True
B. False
questions.verificationRisk: image-dependent; intentionally excluded from score because the screenshot is not sent to /api/ask
questions.rationale: Coverage record only. The original answer is not automatically validated because the required interface image is unavailable to the text-only evaluator.

questions.question: A manipulator mounted on a wheelchair is intended to let the user reach and handle objects. What control relationship does the course associate with this device?
options: A. It is teleoperated by the user
B. It is usable only in one fixed location
C. It is automatically easy because every task is preprogrammed
questions.rationale: Wheelchair-mounted manipulators are user-operated/teleoperated rather than guaranteed preprogrammed devices.

questions.question: An assistive mobile robot must move through a changing home environment while helping its user. Which capability is required in the course description?
options: A. Teleoperation at every moment
B. Autonomous navigation and manipulation
C. A fully structured factory floor
D. No manipulation capability
questions.rationale: Assistive mobile robots need autonomous navigation and manipulation in environments that are not assumed to be structured.

questions.question: Which item is a reusable robotic enabling technology that can be incorporated into an assistive device such as a smart wheelchair?
options: A. Manufacturing
B. Exoskeleton
C. Navigation
D. Automation as a general label
questions.rationale: Navigation is the robotic capability; an exoskeleton is a device category and manufacturing is an application domain.

questions.question: An 83-year-old person has post-stroke hemiplegia and a full-time caregiver who already provides mobility assistance. Under the course's target-user discussion, is this person an ideal user of robotic assistive technology?
options: A. Yes, because age and hemiplegia alone make robotic AT ideal
B. No, the described dependence and existing caregiver support do not match the course's ideal-user rationale
C. Yes, because a caregiver makes every robotic function autonomous
D. The course defines every person with hemiplegia as an ideal user
questions.rationale: The course's target-user logic is not simply diagnosis-based; a full-time caregiver and dependence do not establish the need/profile described for an ideal robotic-AT user.

questions.question: According to the manipulation-aids section, which population is the principal target for a device that assists upper-limb manipulation?
options: A. Lower-limb amputees
B. People with paraplegia only
C. People with quadriplegia
D. People with a lower-limb fracture
questions.rationale: The course identifies quadriplegic users as the target population for manipulation aids.

questions.question: A smart wheelchair lets its rider indicate the desired heading while the onboard system intervenes to avoid collisions. Which combined robotic function best matches the course's typical smart-wheelchair description?
options: A. Autonomous manipulation
B. Wheelchair motor control only
C. Shared-control navigation and obstacle avoidance
D. Autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance
E. Localization and mapping only
questions.rationale: The rider and onboard system share control: navigation intent comes from the user and collision avoidance is assisted by the chair.

questions.question: A young person with tetraplegia has reduced upper-limb function and cannot reliably perform the continuous joystick corrections needed to navigate a standard power chair. Which option best fits the course's mobility-aid hierarchy?
options: A. Manual wheelchair
B. Power-assist wheelchair
C. Smart wheelchair
D. Ordinary power wheelchair
questions.rationale: Reduced propulsion ability calls for powered mobility; difficulty reliably controlling the ordinary powered chair adds the sensor/computer assistance characteristic of a smart wheelchair.

questions.question: In a shared-control wheelchair, the rider chooses the intended direction and the chair's intelligent system prevents a collision. Which statement describes that arrangement?
options: A. The rider controls speed and must independently avoid every obstacle
B. The chair chooses heading while the rider only controls speed
C. The rider sets the heading while the smart wheelchair ensures collision avoidance
questions.rationale: Shared control combines the user's directional command with automated collision-avoidance assistance.

questions.question: A paraplegic resident lives on the third floor of an older building with stairs only. Using the ICF/ICIDH distinctions from the course, which combination is present?
options: A. Impairment plus activity limitation, but no participation restriction
B. No impairment but activity limitation
C. Impairment, activity limitation, and participation restriction
D. Participation restriction without activity limitation
E. Impairment without either activity or participation limitation
questions.rationale: Paraplegia is the impairment; inability to use the stairs is an activity limitation; the inaccessible building creates a participation restriction.

questions.question: A paraplegic resident lives in an accessible high-rise with a working elevator and can reach community facilities. Which classification follows the course's ICF example?
options: A. No impairment but activity limitation
B. Impairment plus activity limitation, without participation restriction
C. Impairment with no activity limitation and no participation restriction
D. Participation restriction without activity limitation
E. All three levels must always be present
questions.rationale: Paraplegia remains an impairment and mobility remains an activity limitation, while the accessible environment removes the described participation restriction.

questions.question: Select all sensor types identified in the smart-wheelchair course material. (Multiple answers.)
options: A. Ultrasound sensors
B. Hall-effect sensors
C. Infrared sensors
D. IMU
E. Force sensors
questions.rationale: The course list includes infrared, IMU, and ultrasound sensors. A bump/tactile contact sensor should not be conflated with a force sensor; the listed force and Hall-effect choices are not the intended answers here.
